findingDetails.title: The removal dropped the dual-export server key while the Vibe session-cleanup hook still calls it, and the fail-open wrapper hides the break
findingDetails.findingClass: dangling consumer of a removed export key
findingDetails.scopeProof: the producer and the packet evidence are inside the 070 review scope; the caller is named as an integration surface because a removal cannot be judged without checking its consumers
findingDetails.claim: dualPlugin now returns exactly { id, setup }, so every Vibe call to sessionCleanupPlugin.server(...) throws and the startup-warning and end-of-session cleanup legs silently never run
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: checked that dualPlugin might keep server non-enumerably (it defines only factory), that three tests assert the key is gone (so the removal is deliberate and host-facing), that the Vibe hook might pass the inner factory rather than the default export (it destructures default at line 77), and that the hook might be disabled by default (the kill switch is SYSTEM_SESSION_CLEANUP_DISABLED, so it is on by default)
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the Vibe hook may be a retired adapter with no live session traffic; its README matrix and kill-switch row record it as an active hook, and no test covers it, so the break would be invisible either way
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: evidence that .vibe/plugins/repo-guards/session-cleanup.mjs is no longer executed by any supported Vibe session, or that a shim restores server before the hook reads it

findingDetails.title: Two of the four re-exported internals in v2-bridge have no importer
findingDetails.findingClass: export surface wider than its consumers
findingDetails.scopeProof: all cited lines are inside the 070 review scope
findingDetails.claim: MAPPED_HOOKS and TOOL_ALIASES are exported but no module imports them, so the export list advertises a contract nothing consumes
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: searched the whole repository for importers of each name; only EVENT_ALIASES and EVENT_MAPPINGS have one, and ARCHITECTURE.md cites MAPPED_HOOKS by symbol rather than importing it
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the export may exist so a future test can assert the mapped-hook set directly, which is the flexibility argument rather than a present consumer
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: an importer of either name outside the reviewed paths

results.summary: the packet records the server-key removal in AC-007 and the code, ARCHITECTURE.md and README.md all state the surviving { id, setup } shape, so the decision and the implementation agree
AC-007's .server( zero-match check searches .opencode/plugins/tests only, so it proves the removal inside the test folder and cannot see the production caller that still calls the removed key

noveltyJustification: both findings are new to the session and neither refines an earlier one; weighted new = 5 (P1) + 1 (P2) = 6 over the iteration's weighted total 6, using the iteration-local convention the prior two records followed

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: a three-phase removal across runtime code, CI pins and docs, with an export contract shared by every plugin file and by at least one non-OpenCode runtime

targetSelection.selectionReason: the D4 focus named the surviving v2 adapter and its removed server key; a removal finding is only checkable against the consumers of the removed key, so the search continued to the one caller outside OpenCode
omittedHighRiskTargets: plugin runtime behavior under a live OpenCode 2 host is not executed in a review iteration
the .vibe hook is read, not run, so the thrown TypeError is inferred from the export shape rather than observed
